scope: Human identity-affecting altruism, contingent instrumental non-elimination, goal drift, cooperation/commitment and practical autonomy against AI dominance
record_count_caveat: C01-C14 241 IDs verified before adding; C15 will be counted only after collision audit. These are different publications, NOT all human empirical samples or full-text studies.
source_selection: Publisher origination prioritized, avoid recycled second-hand citations; paper-by-paper accessible text grade and first-repo discovery unknown.

records.original_title: No Harm Done? An Experimental Approach to the Nonidentity Problem
records.original_evidence_scope: Two human online dictator-game experimental arms. Baseline 177 dictators (354 total participants), mean B transfer $0.238. Identity-sensitive version 176 dictators with eleven potential B recipients per A (1936 potential recipients), mean transfer $0.155; p<0.001. B's membership in eligible payout recipient set changes with A's donation amount.
records.adversarial_countercase: A transfers less when her choice also controls which B participates; self-identity/recipient tracking affects apparent altruism.
records.scope_limit: This is monetary selection of real recipients, NOT destruction or actual nonexistence of anyone; 1936 B recipients cannot be treated as independent dictators; experimental design modifies social context beyond literal identity continuity; publication online 2021 / print 2022 same study.

records.original_title: The Superintelligent Will: Motivation and Instrumental Rationality in Advanced Artificial Agents
records.original_evidence_scope: Original philosophical argument for orthogonality and instrumental convergence (a broad class of final goals may lead rational powerful agents to seek convergent intermediate resources, survival and goal integrity).
records.adversarial_countercase: Goals and intelligence are not automatically linked; no reason mere strength entails spontaneous human/other-regard.
records.scope_limit: Thesis has qualifications, not formal proof all powerful agents always eliminate B. Criticized by Gallow 2024/2025 and Southan et al 2025; no AGI empirical samples.

records.original_evidence_scope: Original decision-theoretic model finds biases toward reduced randomness, goal/desire preservation and actions leaving more future choice; not generic convergence toward all other Bostrom intermediate goals.
records.adversarial_countercase: Rationality alone does not imply all instrumental-convergence means; preserving future option sets is stronger claim than unconditional protection of someone else's exit.
records.scope_limit: Published online Apr 2024, print 2025, ONE publication. Publisher paywall; proof conditions and assumptions not independently reconstructed.

records.original_authors: Rhys Southan; Helena Ward; Jen Semler
records.original_title: A timing problem for instrumental convergence
records.original_evidence_scope: Original open philosophical argument: a means-rational agent's changing its final goal need not breach any obligation to pursue the earlier goal after that goal is abandoned; goal content integrity is not guaranteed by means-rationality alone.
records.adversarial_countercase: A future agent retaining a preference to spare B does not entail its future self keeps that preference after self-revision; a strong counterpoint to inevitable goal preservation.
records.scope_limit: An actively planning current agent could disprefer a goal change when evaluated with its present utility; timing-problem critique is an argument, not universal theorem requiring goals to change or demonstrating agent persistence.

records.original_title: The elimination cascade: why instrumental convergence may favor preservation over elimination
records.original_evidence_scope: Original 2026 formal abstract claims AND/OR dependency-graph cascades and uncertain indirect dependencies can make irreversible elimination of seemingly useless entities risky to powerful agent's own complex goals; mentions game theoretic Shapley cooperation mapping.
records.adversarial_countercase: Surprisingly close original overlap with Project EI: reasons of long-run agent self-interest can favor not eliminating supposedly unneeded counterpart.
records.scope_limit: FULL PAPER PAYWALLED; exact theorem assumptions/proof/effective uncertainty thresholds not inspected; Springer declares no datasets and no code. This is CONDITIONAL/INSTRUMENTAL preservation and NOT universal B-specific voluntary coexistence; non-zero hidden dependency assumes outcome cost the dominant agent fears.

records.original_evidence_scope: Original open philosophical/evolutionary account distinguishing contractual third-party, reputation-backed, emotional and self-enforcing commitment. Discusses bounded cooperation and distributional temptation/monopolizing gains.
records.adversarial_countercase: Credible contract may protect B while credible external sanctions remain; 'committed protection' is not evidence powerful A voluntarily values expendable B after third-party power disappears.
records.scope_limit: No new experimental dataset; historical origin account conceptual, not evidence of AGI welfare-preserving motives. Conditions need explicit time and future enforcement scope.

records.original_title: Obsolescence without hostility: optimization, uniformity, and the erosion of human meaning in a post-AI world
records.original_evidence_scope: Original discussion argues that even without direct hostility, humans ceasing to be necessary may lose outcome-affecting agency; optimization-driven uniformity can undermine meaningful participation.
records.adversarial_countercase: A can leave B alive and materially secure yet deplete B's causal agency/autonomous option space: coexistence metric must demand executable agency, not absence of direct killing.
records.scope_limit: Article speculates on technological horizon and meaning; does not prove literal extinction, physical elimination or normative moral status of all agents. Full paper paywalled and states no datasets.

records.original_authors: Weihua Zhou; Xin Lin; Lei Fu; Ying Tang; Cangyu Jin
records.original_title: Why human–AI collaboration fails: An operational contestability framework
records.original_evidence_scope: Original operational framework: cognitive asymmetry, dynamic delegation, meta-learning and Encoding-Habituation-Closure can erode practical human opportunity to challenge an AI decision, even if human formally in the loop.
records.adversarial_countercase: A formal refusal button/voice may remain while intervention is late, infeasible or too costly to be useful; assess effective contestability before A execution.
records.scope_limit: Publisher subscription preview, no direct causal field test supplied. Does not infer intrinsic AI mind, agent goals or guaranteed avoidance of exploitation.

records.original_authors: Zhuoqiong Chen; Ruixin Wang; Jichuan Zong
records.original_title: Pre-commitment in bargaining with endogenous credibility
records.original_evidence_scope: Original modified ultimatum lab experiments letting responder set minimum acceptable offer MAO and cost of backing down CBD. Nearly 40% set CBD materially below MAO (partially credible), although fully credible promises induced higher offers.
records.adversarial_countercase: Agent-optimal precommitment is not inevitable even in small games. Partial credible commitments may reveal other-regarding concerns, yet differ from keeping B's revocable veto under unilateral A takeover.
records.scope_limit: Human bargaining with responder rejection power and material reciprocity, not unmonitorable total-power future AI; publisher partial original and author journal-index metadata, full paper paywalled.
